t: This is a statue of the Romantic poet John Keats, standing in Moorfields, Moorgate. Martin Jennings sculpted it as a larger than life-size copy of a life mask of Keats, taken when he was twenty-one. The place matters because Keats was the son of an ostler at the nearby inn, The Swan and Hoop. The Lord Mayor of London, Michael Mainelli, unveiled it on 31 October 2024, the 229th anniversary of Keats's birth. Jennings also made the statues of John Betjeman at St Pancras and Mary Seacole at St Thomas' Hospital.
